So I'll centre each protein per site, using the training-fold site means after imputation, so the L2 logistic model learns within-cohort differences instead of cohort offsets. Scoring is within cohort, so differences in protein levels between the four CSF cohorts only add noise when the model is trained on the pooled data. This change uses `site` only for harmonization: it centres each protein's log2 values on that protein's median within each site, which removes cohort offsets while keeping the within-site differences that separate AD from non-AD.

The four CSF cohorts differ in pre-analytics and MS runs, so site offsets in protein levels are noise for a model that is scored within site. Before the model sees the data, I subtract each protein's per-site median (computed without labels, on all items). This removes those offsets so the L2 logistic model learns disease differences shared across cohorts instead of site differences.

Scoring happens within each site, but the classifier currently learns on pooled data. Cohort-level offsets in protein intensity (from pre-analytics, run order or instrument) can therefore pull the weights toward proteins that separate sites rather than AD from non-AD. Centring and scaling every protein within each site, using training-fold statistics only, removes those offsets, so the L2 logistic model learns only from within-site contrasts. This is exactly the comparison that gets scored.

The four CSF cohorts were measured separately, so each protein has its own offset per site. Those offsets add variance the pooled classifier has to work through, and they don't help because scoring is within site. This change centres each protein on its per-site median in `featurize`. It uses only the site label and no outcome labels, and leaves the rest of the pipeline unchanged.

Scoring is AUROC within each of the four CSF cohorts, so differences between sites in protein levels are only noise. In the pooled model they can also mix with the different case rates per site. It uses no labels, and missing values stay missing so the existing filter and imputation in `fit_predict` work as before. This change subtracts each site's per-protein median from the imputed log2 features, using only labels-free site metadata, so the logistic regression learns from within-site variation. For test items, the shift is constant inside each site, so it can't distort within-site rankings. The gain comes from a cleaner training signal.

AUROC is scored within each site, so differences in protein levels between the four CSF cohorts (pre-analytics, instrument runs) only add noise when the classifier is trained on pooled data.
